link's segments for one species in a set of groups, with flow and access, for grading

Source: R/link_segments.R
knw_link_segments.Rd

The segment table a grade is written on: every streams row of the groups, with streams_access.access_<sp>, the species' habitat flags (re-gated on access, stored flags beside), and wet's picked annual flow. Own flow is one join; the parent fallback knw_link_flow() applies per visit (the nearest primary-flow segment on the main line or the segment's own line) runs only on the segments with no own flow, so millions of segments read in one pass.

Usage

knw_link_segments(
  conn,
  schema,
  species,
  wsg,
  parent_fallback = TRUE,
  gradient = "segment"
)

Arguments

conn

a DBI connection to a database holding schema and discharge.

schema

character(1) link persist schema.

species

character(1) species code.

wsg

character watershed group codes.

parent_fallback

logical(1) run the parent fallback for segments with no own picked flow.

gradient

character(1) where gradient comes from (#120): "segment", the segment's own (link's gradient, token grad-seg); "parent", its minimal-network parent's, from <schema>.streams_parent (link#444, grad-parent), checked by knw_parent_read() first; "fwa", its Freshwater Atlas segment's (fwa_stream_networks_sp.gradient on linear_feature_id; no link segment crosses an Atlas segment, link#444). A segment with no row in the source stops the read.

Value

A tibble, one row per segment: id_segment, watershed_group_code, linear_feature_id, blue_line_key, downstream_route_measure, upstream_route_measure, length_metre, edge_type, stream_order, waterbody_key, gradient, channel_width, channel_width_source, wscode, localcode, access, accessible, spawning, rearing, lake_rearing, wetland_rearing (re-gated), *_stored, mad_pick, pick_source, flow_from.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), bigint = "numeric")
seg <- knw_link_segments(conn, "fresh_default", "CH", c("BULK", "MORR"))
} # }
